get.description: List all calendars in a project associated with the Scheduling/Programming tool. V2.1 returns only source intervals (parent_interval_id IS NULL) and exposes the availability JSON on Exception intervals. Use the Show Project API when you need the project time zone to interpret UTC timestamps or values expressed in project time.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort by supported fields. Accepts comma separated values to sort by multiple fields. Order is ascending by default, prefix field with '-' for descending

Link.description: Link header for the first, prev, next, and the last page links

calendar_id.description: The unique identifier for the calendar

is_global.description: Indicates if the calendar is available to all projects in the company

hours_per_day.description: The number of working hours in a day

days_per_week.description: The number of working days in a week

days_per_month.description: The number of working days in a month

calendar_intervals.description: The intervals associated with this calendar

interval_id.description: The unique identifier for the interval

recurrent_start_date.description: The start of a recurring interval. The day of week and time values are in project time zone
recurrent_start_date.example: on Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri at 17:00

recurrent_end_date.description: The end of a recurring interval. The day of week and time values are in project time zone
recurrent_end_date.example: on Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri at 18:00

start_date.description: The start date and time of the interval in UTC (ISO 8601 format)

end_date.description: The end date and time of the interval in UTC (ISO 8601 format)

is_working.description: A flag to indicate whether this period is considered working time

availability.description: JSON array of working slots within an Exception interval. Only present on Exception intervals.

is_archived.description: Indicates if the calendar is archived

created_at.description: The creation timestamp of the calendar in UTC (ISO 8601 format)

updated_at.description: The last update timestamp of the calendar in UTC (ISO 8601 format)

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

Python3
x-code-samples.content:
import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

conn.request("GET", "/rest/v2.1/companies/1234/projects/5678/calendars?filters%5Bcalendar_id%5D=SOME_STRING_VALUE&filters%5Bname%5D=SOME_STRING_VALUE&filters%5Bis_global%5D=SOME_BOOLEAN_VALUE&sort=SOME_STRING_VALUE&page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE&per_page=SOME_INTEGER_VALUE")

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))
